entries.definition: and other similar things; and so on
entries.example: Bring pencils, paper, notebooks, etc.

entries.definition: used to introduce one or more examples
entries.example: Some fruits, e.g. apples and oranges, are easy to find.

entries.definition: used to explain exactly what you mean
entries.example: Meet me at noon, i.e. 12:00 p.m.

entries.definition: as quickly as reasonably possible
entries.example: Please send me the document ASAP.

entries.definition: used when giving someone information they may find useful
entries.example: FYI, the meeting starts at nine.

entries.definition: a common document file format that preserves layout
entries.example: The article is available as a PDF.

entries.definition: computer technology designed to perform tasks associated with human intelligence
entries.example: AI can help students practice language skills.

entries.definition: the United States government agency responsible for civilian space exploration
entries.example: NASA studies Earth and space.

entries.definition: used to introduce a new or additional topic in conversation
entries.example: By the way, have you finished your homework?

entries.definition: used before saying what you truly think or feel
entries.example: To be honest, I found the test difficult.

entries.definition: until the present time
entries.example: So far, everything is going well.

entries.definition: used to show that something is expected, obvious, or certainly allowed
entries.example: Of course you can ask questions.

entries.definition: something that is very easy to do
entries.learner_note: This expression is not literally about cake.
entries.chinese: 小菜一碟；非常容易的事情
entries.example: The homework was a piece of cake.

entries.definition: feeling slightly sick or unwell
entries.learner_note: It describes someone's health, not the weather.
entries.example: I'm feeling under the weather today.

entries.definition: a way of wishing someone good luck before a performance
entries.learner_note: It does not mean that you want the person to be injured.
entries.example: You have a performance tonight? Break a leg!

entries.definition: to stop working on something for the day
entries.example: We've done enough work. Let's call it a day.

entries.definition: to begin studying seriously
entries.chinese: 开始认真学习；用功读书
entries.example: I have an exam tomorrow, so I need to hit the books.

entries.definition: suddenly and unexpectedly
entries.example: She called me out of the blue.

entries.definition: to watch or take care of someone or something
entries.example: Could you keep an eye on my bag?

entries.definition: to begin to understand how to do something
entries.example: You'll get the hang of it after some practice.

entries.definition: to search for information in a book, dictionary, or other source
entries.example: Look up the word in the dictionary.

entries.definition: to take care of someone or something
entries.example: She looks after her younger brother.

entries.definition: to stop trying to do something
entries.example: Don't give up just because the exercise is difficult.

entries.definition: to discover or learn information
entries.example: I need to find out what happened.

entries.definition: to understand or solve something
entries.example: Can you figure out the answer?

entries.definition: to make a device or machine begin operating
entries.example: Please turn on the computer.

entries.definition: to make a device or machine stop operating
entries.example: Turn off the lights before you leave.

entries.definition: to lift something, collect someone, or learn something informally
entries.example: She picked up some Chinese while living in Beijing.

entries.definition: to delay doing something until a later time
entries.example: Don't put off your homework until tomorrow.

entries.definition: to meet someone unexpectedly or encounter a problem
entries.example: I ran into an old friend yesterday.

entries.definition: to continue doing something
entries.example: Please carry on with your work.

entries.definition: to find or meet someone or something unexpectedly
entries.example: I came across an interesting article.
